text:
priya_k: ACME prod is seeing repeated 429s on their Dedicated pool ded-nyc-1 — customer reports it started ~2025-08-12T20:30Z. They say requests succeed sometimes, then throttle for minutes.

oncall_bot: ALERT ded-nyc-1: KV_CACHE_EVICTION_SPIKE (rate=178/s) — triggered at 2025-08-12T20:31:10Z.

ops_james: can you paste a sample request id + the error payload? need to triage whether this is auth/quotas or runtime throttling.

priya_k: request ids: r_0a1b2c3d, r_0a1b2c3e. customer supplied this curl + response:
```bash
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -H "Authorization: Bearer <redacted>" -d '{"model":"rw-gig-8k","input":"<40k tokens chat...>"}'
```
response: `HTTP/1.1 429`
```json
{"error":"capacity.throttle","code":"kv_cache_limit","detail":"kv_cache_eviction_rate_high: tenant=acme-prod, pool=ded-nyc-1"}
```

sasha_w: looks like KV cache thrash from long-context workloads. Long-history chats create lots of unique KV entries; eviction churn causes memory fragmentation and spikes in eviction rate -> runtime starts returning capacity.throttle to keep SLOs. we should collect heap/kv metrics from the nodes and check `kv_cache_size`, `kv_fragmentation`, `kv_eviction_rate`, and `pending_queue_length`.

dev_sharma: quick note on autoscaler: current policy for ded-nyc-1 uses metric `avg_qps` with min_replicas=2 max_replicas=8. qps didn't jump because requests are long and batching holds requests, so autoscaler didn't see the short qps spike. autoscaler logs show no scale-out decision between 20:25-20:35Z.

priya_k: customer confirmed workload pattern: many active chats with long contexts (30k-50k tokens) and lots of unique conversation IDs. They also recently increased model size to rw-gig-8k which increases per-session KV footprint (more layers -> larger KV).

sasha_w: proposed mitigation (short-term):
1) enable tenant-level soft cap bump: `kv_cache_limit_multiplier=1.5` for acme-prod.
2) flip eviction policy to LRU-heavy (reduce fragmentation).
3) enable `eviction_backoff_ms=50` to avoid immediate re-entrancy thrash.
Execute via admin API:
```bash
# temp bump for tenant
curl -X POST https://control.redwood.ai/admin/dedicated/config \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer <admin-token>" \
  -d '{"tenant":"acme-prod","kv_cache_limit_multiplier":1.5,"eviction_policy":"lru","eviction_backoff_ms":50}'
```
These are safe short-term changes, should reduce evictions while we debug root cause.

dev_sharma: longer-term autoscaler change: bump the pool by +2 GPUs now and switch autoscale metric to include `kv_eviction_rate` (or `pending_queue_length`) so we respond to memory pressure, not just qps. I'll prepare the scaling plan.

ops_james: will kick off +2 GPU bump in ded-nyc-1 and enable debug logging for kv (pprof endpoints). ETA 20m. creating ticket: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/INF-8342 (ops will own immediate bump).

priya_k: updated ACME with mitigation plan and ETA. asked them to avoid large-batch imports for now.

sasha_w: please collect these artifacts once bump is in place:
- `/var/log/runtime/kv_evictions.log` (last 1h)
- node heap profiles (pprof)
- `kubectl top` / GPU memory snapshots
- runtime metrics around `kv_fragmentation` and `kv_eviction_rate`
Also run repro: single session with 45k tokens, then repeated new sessions to simulate unique keys. we need to reproduce eviction spike locally.

ops_james: done - bump applied at 20:52Z. debug logging on. attaching logs to ticket.

priya_k: ACME says errors dropped after ~7 minutes post-bump. still monitoring. I'll keep customer posted and mark as Escalation->Pending Follow-up.

sasha_w: next steps: eng-runtime to analyze logs and heap profiles, eng-infra to update autoscaler metric, product to discuss longer-term tenant caps and guidance on long-context workloads. assign owners: sasha_w (runtime), dev_sharma (infra), priya_k (support).

priya_k: thanks everyone — I'll run a 30-min follow-up sync with ACME and update INF-8342 with artifacts. :thumbsup:
